mainTopic: The penalties for remarrying on a flawed גט, and the גמרא on dating a גט by a kingdom and writing the correct place
overview: This amud finishes the long משנה about a woman who remarried based on a flawed גט. She loses her rights to תרומה or מעשר and to her כתובה, and if the husbands die, each brother must do חליצה but none may do יבום. The משנה applies the same penalties to a גט with the wrong name or city. It also applies them to co-wives who remarried by mistake when the ערוה or יבמה turned out to be an איילונית, and to a case where the scribe swapped the גט and the receipt. רבי אלעזר disagrees and says a גט found with the husband only after some time is still valid. The גמרא then explains that the 'kingdom that is not legitimate' is רומי. עולא says a גט is dated by the kingdom to keep peace with the government, and the harsh penalties fit רבי מאיר's view that any change in the חכמים' set wording invalidates a גט. The גמרא shows why each dating case in the משנה is needed. It explains that 'he was in the east and wrote in the west' is about the scribe, who must write the place where he actually sits. A new statement of שמואל begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A בת לוי or בת כהן loses her food rights
steps.stepSummary: The list of penalties continues. A בת לוי loses the right to eat מעשר, and a בת כהן loses the right to eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she was the daughter of a לוי, she is disqualified from eating מעשר. If she was the daughter of a כהן, she is disqualified from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is in the middle of a list of penalties for a woman who remarried based on a flawed גט. These two items cover the daughter of a לוי and the daughter of a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list started on the previous daf. It said that a בת ישראל in this situation becomes disqualified from marrying a כהן. Now the משנה adds matching penalties for a בת לוי and a בת כהן. Each one loses the holy food she would normally be allowed to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic teaching that the גמרא then discusses
Daughter of a Levite
The tithe given to the Levites
Daughter of a Kohen
The holy portion of produce given to the כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the middle of a long list that started on the previous daf. Each item answers the question: what does this woman lose?

phrases.english: A Levite's daughter – [is disqualified] from the tithe.
A Kohen's daughter – [is disqualified] from terumah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of penalties that began on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בת לוי loses מעשר and a בת כהן loses תרומה because of this improper remarriage.

steps.title: No one inherits her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The heirs of neither husband inherit her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heirs of this husband and the heirs of that husband do not inherit her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more money penalty. Neither husband's heirs can collect her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the list, the משנה said she gets no כתובה from either husband. Now it goes one step further. Even the heirs connected to each marriage cannot inherit rights to that כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Heirs, or those who inherit
The marriage contract and the money it promises

phrases.english: And the heirs of this one do not
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' mean the first husband and the second husband.

phrases.english: and the heirs of that one
inherit her marriage contract.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין יוֹרְשִׁין שֶׁל זֶה וְיוֹרְשִׁין שֶׁל זֶה יוֹרְשִׁים כְּתוּבָּתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another penalty to the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither husband's heirs inherit her כתובה.

steps.title: If the husbands die: חליצה but no יבום
steps.stepSummary: If both husbands die without children, each husband's brother does חליצה. Neither brother does יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they die, the brother of this husband and the brother of that husband do חליצה, but they do not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list of penalties. It says what happens if the husbands die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she was connected to both men, each brother must do חליצה to release her. But neither brother may marry her through יבום. This fits the whole list: she keeps every burden of both marriages but gets none of the benefits.

keyTerms.meaning: They do חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
They do יבום, marrying the brother's widow
His brother

steps.whatToRemember: The overall pattern: a woman who remarried on a flawed גט must leave both men. She loses all the benefits of both marriages, and she still needs a release (a גט, or חליצה) from each side.

phrases.english: And if they died –

phrases.aramaic: אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: the brother of this one and the brother of that one
perform chalitzah, and do not perform levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מֵתוּ – אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה חוֹלְצִין, וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last item in the list of penalties.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both brothers-in-law do חליצה and none may do יבום.

steps.title: A wrong name or city in the גט brings the same penalties
steps.stepSummary: If the גט changed his name, her name, his city, or her city, and she remarried, she must leave both men. All the penalties listed above apply to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he changed his name, her name, the name of his city, or the name of her city, she must leave both this man and that man. All these penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new kind of flawed גט, one with the wrong names or cities. It applies the whole list of penalties to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the flaws were in how the גט was dated, or in writing the wrong place where it was written ('he was in the east and wrote in the west'). Here, the flaw is in the names of the people or their cities. The משנה does not repeat the list. It simply says that all the same 'ways' (penalties) apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: He changed (wrote something different)
The name of his city
She must leave both this one and that one
These ways (the penalties already listed)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that writing the names and places correctly in a גט is treated just as seriously as the dating rules.

phrases.english: If he changed his name, or her name,
the name of his city, or the name of her city –
she must leave this one and that one,
phrases.notes: This is the case where she remarried based on this גט. She must leave both the first husband and the second.

phrases.english: and all these ways apply to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁינָּה שְׁמוֹ, וּשְׁמָהּ, שֵׁם עִירוֹ, וְשֵׁם עִירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the penalty list just completed to a new kind of flawed גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט with a changed name or city brings all the same penalties as the wrongly dated גט.

steps.title: Opening a new rule about the צרות of עריות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new rule: 'All the עריות about which they said their צרות are permitted.' The rest of the sentence comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the forbidden relatives about whom they said 'their rival wives are permitted'...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next rule. This line only opens the case, and the rule itself comes in the following lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some women count as an ערוה to their dead husband's brother, such as his wife's sister. When that is so, there is no יבום, and her צרות (her husband's other wives) are also free to marry without יבום or חליצה. The משנה is about to connect this case to the penalties it just listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives one is forbidden to marry
Their rival wives (the other wives of the same husband)
Permitted

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Don't look for the ruling yet; it comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: All the forbidden relatives about whom they said
'their rival wives are permitted' –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from flawed גטין to a new, related case about צרות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the case of עריות whose צרות are permitted. The ruling follows.

steps.title: Co-wives who remarried, but the forbidden wife was an איילונית
steps.stepSummary: The צרות of an ערוה remarried without יבום or חליצה. Then the ערוה turned out to be an איילונית. The צרות must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: These co-wives went and married other men. Then the forbidden relatives were found to be women who cannot have children. She must leave both this man and that man, and all these penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the sentence it started in step 5. It gives a case where co-wives remarried because they thought they were free, and that turned out to be a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the צרה of an ערוה is free from יבום, so she may marry anyone. But here the ערוה was an איילונית, so her marriage to the dead brother was never valid. That means the co-wife was never really the צרה of an ערוה. She still needed יבום or חליצה, so her new marriage was a mistake, and she is penalized like the woman with the bad גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Co-wives, other wives married to the same husband
A woman who never physically developed and cannot have children
She must leave this one and that one (both men)
Literally 'the ways'. Here it means the list of penalties

steps.confusionAlert: The word אלו ('these') in 'these were found to be איילוניות' does not mean the co-wives. It means the forbidden relatives. The co-wives are the ones who must leave.

phrases.english: These co-wives went and got married,
and these were found to be women unable to have children –
phrases.notes: 'These' means the forbidden relatives from step 5, not the co-wives.

phrases.english: she must leave this one and that one,
phrases.notes: She leaves the new husband, and she also cannot do יבום with the brother.

phrases.english: and all these penalties apply to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sentence begun in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ערוה turns out to be an איילונית, her co-wives were never exempt. If they remarried, they must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.

steps.title: A יבם married his יבמה, who turned out to be an איילונית
steps.stepSummary: A יבם did יבום with one widow, and her co-wife remarried. Then the widow he married turned out to be an איילונית. The co-wife must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone marries his יבמה, and her co-wife went and married another man, and then this יבמה was found to be an איילונית, the co-wife must leave both men, and all these penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case of a co-wife who remarried because she thought she was free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, when the יבם does יבום with one widow, the other widow is free to marry anyone. But the widow he married was an איילונית, so her marriage to the dead brother was never valid, and the יבום with her did not count. So the co-wife was never released. Her new marriage was a mistake, and she gets the same penalties.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries (brings in)
His יבמה, his brother's widow, who needs יבום
To another man

phrases.english: One who marries his brother's widow,
and her co-wife went and married another man,
and this one was found to be a woman unable to have children;
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the widow the יבם married, not the co-wife.

phrases.english: she must leave this one and that one,
and all these penalties apply to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case to step 6, with the same reasoning and the same ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the יבמה who had יבום turns out to be an איילונית, her co-wife was never released. If the co-wife remarried, she must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.

steps.title: The scribe mixes up the גט and the receipt
steps.stepSummary: A סופר wrote a גט for the husband and a שובר for the wife. He mixed them up, and each spouse handed the other the wrong paper.
steps.simpleTranslation: A scribe wrote a גט for the man and a receipt for the woman. He made a mistake and gave the גט to the woman and the receipt to the man, and they gave them to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets up a new case. This step only describes what happened. The ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband was supposed to hand the wife a גט. The wife was supposed to hand him a שובר saying she was paid her כתובה. Because of the mix-up, she handed him the גט and he handed her the receipt. A גט only works when the husband gives it to the wife, so no divorce happened at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A scribe who writes documents
A receipt. Here the wife signs that she received her כתובה money
He made a mistake
To each other

phrases.english: A scribe wrote a bill of divorce for the man,
and a receipt for the woman;
and he made a mistake and gave the bill of divorce to the woman,
and the receipt to the man,
and they gave them to each other;
phrases.notes: So the wife handed the גט to the husband, which is backwards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the יבום cases to a new kind of mistake: a mix-up of documents
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Describes the case only: the papers were swapped, so the wrong person handed over the גט.

steps.title: The mix-up is discovered, and she must leave both men
steps.stepSummary: Later the גט turns up in the husband's hand and the שובר in the wife's. She was never divorced, so if she remarried she must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later on, the גט is found in the man's hand and the receipt in the woman's hand. She must leave both this man and that man, and all these penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ruling for the case set up in step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the papers are found in the wrong hands, everyone realizes the divorce never happened. She remarried while still married to her first husband. So she must leave both her first husband and her new husband, and every penalty from the earlier list applies.

keyTerms.meaning: After some time, later on
From the hand of, in the possession of

steps.whatToRemember: In every case in this section, she remarried because of a mistake that was discovered later. The משנה gives the same result each time: she leaves both men, and all the penalties apply.

phrases.english: And after some time, the bill of divorce is
coming out of the man's hand,
and the receipt from the woman's hand –
she must leave this one and that one,
phrases.notes: The משנה assumes she had already remarried, so she leaves her first husband and her second husband.

phrases.english: and all these penalties apply to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְאַחַר זְמַן הֲרֵי הַגֵּט יוֹצֵא מִיַּד הָאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swapped papers mean there was no divorce. A woman who remarried must leave both men, and all the penalties apply.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: it depends on when the גט turns up
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that if the גט is found with the husband right away, it is not a גט. If it is found only after some time, it is a valid גט, because the first husband cannot take away the second husband's rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: If the גט turns up in the husband's hand right away, it is not a valid גט. If it turns up only after some time, it is a valid גט. The first husband does not have the power to wipe out the rights of the second husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by quoting רבי אלעזר. He disagrees with the strict ruling in Step 9 when time has passed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding the גט right away shows it was never really handed over. If time has passed, we assume she did receive it properly and the husband later got it back. We do not let the first husband's claim undo the second marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: Right away, immediately
After some time
His right or claim

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
If it turned up right away
phrases.notes: 'It' is the גט, turning up in the husband's hand, like the case in Step 9.

phrases.english: this is not a valid גט;
if it turned up after some time,
this is a valid גט –
it is not in the power of the first husband
to destroy the right of the second husband.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: a גט found back with the husband right away is invalid. One found after some time is valid, because the first husband cannot ruin the second marriage.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting view on the mixed-up גט case from Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found right away: not a גט. Found after time: a valid גט, since the first husband cannot cancel the second husband's rights.

steps.title: What is 'a kingdom that is not legitimate'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה meant by 'a kingdom that is not legitimate.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'a kingdom that is not legitimate'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about a phrase from the משנה: a גט dated by a kingdom that is not legitimate. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a גט dated by 'a kingdom that is not legitimate' as a problem. The גמרא first wants to know exactly which kingdom that is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A kingdom that is not legitimate

phrases.english: גמרא:
What is 'a kingdom that is not legitimate'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא, going back to an earlier phrase in the משנה.

steps.title: It means רומי
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רומי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רומי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: the kingdom meant is רומי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the משנה's case is a גט dated by the years of רומי while it was written in a land רומי does not rule. That is why it causes trouble with the local government (see steps 15 and 18).

keyTerms.meaning: Rome, the Roman Empire

phrases.english: Rome.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'kingdom that is not legitimate' is רומי.

steps.title: Why call רומי 'not legitimate'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רומי is called a kingdom that is not legitimate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called a kingdom that is not legitimate?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know it is רומי, the גמרא asks what makes רומי 'not legitimate.' This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רומי was a powerful empire. So the גמרא wants to know what is lacking in it that earns this label.

keyTerms.meaning: And why?
Calls it

phrases.english: And why does it call it
a kingdom that is not legitimate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question on the answer in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רומי is called 'not legitimate.'

steps.title: They have no script or language of their own
steps.stepSummary: רומי is called 'not legitimate' because it has no writing system and no language of its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they have neither their own script nor their own language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רומי lacks its own script and language, so it is called 'not legitimate.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kingdom without its own writing or language is described as not fully proper. That is the source of the name, which the משנה uses when discussing the date in a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Script, a writing system
Language

phrases.english: Because they do not have
neither a script, nor a language.
phrases.notes: He means a script and language of their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין לָהֶם לֹא כְּתָב, וְלֹא לָשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רומי has no script or language of its own.

steps.title: עולא: dating by the kingdom keeps peace with the government
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the חכמים required dating a גט by the local kingdom to keep peaceful relations with the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Why did they institute writing the kingdom's date in a גט? To keep peace with the kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the reason behind the rule that a גט is dated by the years of the kingdom: to keep the government happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dating a גט by the government's years is not a Torah requirement. It is a rule of the חכמים, made for the practical reason of avoiding trouble with the authorities.

keyTerms.meaning: They instituted, a rule made by the חכמים
Peace with the government

phrases.english: עולא said:
For what reason did they institute
the kingdom in bills of divorce?
phrases.notes: He means writing the date by the years of the ruling kingdom.

phrases.english: Because of peace with the kingdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: מִפְּנֵי מָה תִּיקְּנוּ מַלְכוּת בְּגִיטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what the kingdom is to why a גט is dated by a kingdom at all.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dating a גט by the kingdom is a rule of the חכמים, made for the sake of peace with the government.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reason sets up the next challenge. If the rule is only for keeping peace, are the harsh penalties too strong?

steps.title: Such harsh penalties just for peace with the government?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the rule is only for keeping peace with the government, would the חכמים really make the woman leave her husband and make her child a ממזר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And just because of peace with the kingdom, she must leave her husband and the child is a ממזר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא's reason. A light reason like peace with the government seems too weak to produce such severe results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה put the wrong-kingdom date case among the cases where she must leave and the child is a ממזר. But if the rule exists only to avoid trouble with the government, these heavy penalties seem far out of proportion.

keyTerms.meaning: She must leave her husband
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who cannot marry into the regular community

phrases.english: And because of peace with the kingdom –
she must leave, and the child is a mamzer?!

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not questioning whether the rule exists. It is asking why breaking a rule made only for peace with the government gets such severe penalties.
steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם שְׁלוֹם מַלְכוּת תֵּצֵא וְהַוָּלָד מַמְזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reason in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that the rule is only for peace with the government, combined with the משנה's harsh penalties.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule made for a light, practical reason should not lead to making the woman leave her husband and making her child a ממזר.

steps.title: Yes, because רבי מאיר is strict about any change to a גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר is consistent. He holds that anyone who changes the wording the חכמים set for a גט makes the child a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. רבי מאיר follows his own reasoning. As רב המנונא said in the name of עולא: רבי מאיר used to say that anyone who changes the set wording the חכמים made for a גט, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. It says yes, the harsh result is real, because this is רבי מאיר's general rule for any change to a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 asked how a rule made only for peace with the government could be strong enough to make a child a ממזר. The answer is that רבי מאיר does not judge each detail on its own. Once the חכמים set a form for a גט, changing it makes the גט invalid, so any remarriage based on it produces a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
Following his own reasoning; consistent with his other view
One who changes
The set formula (literally, the 'coin') the חכמים minted
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the general community

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי מאיר, changing the חכמים' set wording of a גט makes the גט invalid, so a child from a later marriage is a ממזר, even when the reason behind the wording was only peace with the government.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule made by the חכמים, once fixed as part of how a גט is written, can carry the full weight of an invalid divorce.

phrases.english: Yes, Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning –
phrases.notes: The 'yes' answers the question from step 16: the woman really must leave her husband and the child really is a ממזר.

phrases.english: as Rav Hamnuna said in the name of Ulla,
Rabbi Meir would say:
anyone who changes from the formula
phrases.notes: Literally 'the coin.' Like a coin stamped in a fixed form, the חכמים set a fixed wording for a גט.

phrases.english: that the Sages set for bills of divorce –
the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by accepting its conclusion and grounding it in רבי מאיר's general view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the harsh result and showing it fits the speaker's consistent general principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rule made only for peace with the government should not be strong enough to make a child a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי מאיר, any change from the חכמים' set wording of a גט invalidates it, so the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs both the illegitimate kingdom and מדי and יון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of dating by the Greek kingdom and says each case is needed. A kingdom that rules now is a problem, but one might think old kingdoms like מדי and יון are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'by the kingdom of יון.' And each case is needed. If the משנה had taught only the kingdom that is not legitimate, I would say that is a problem because it rules now. But the kingdom of מדי and the kingdom of יון? What was, was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and starts explaining why it lists several separate dating cases. This step gives the first reason and sets up the next ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about dating a גט is that the local government will be upset. A kingdom that rules today, like רומי, could cause real anger, but kingdoms that are already gone might seem harmless. So the משנה must also mention מדי and יון to teach that they are forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is needed; each case teaches something new
It had taught us
A kingdom that is not legitimate (רומי, from steps 12 to 14)
It rules; it is currently in power
What was, was; it is in the past

steps.confusionAlert: This is a צריכא: the גמרא is not doubting the rule. It is showing why the משנה had to spell out each case instead of giving just one.

phrases.english: 'In the name of the Greek kingdom.' And it is necessary;
for if it had taught us only a kingdom that is not legitimate –
that is because it rules now;
but the kingdom of Media and the kingdom of Greece –
what was, was;
phrases.notes: He means those kingdoms are already gone, so one might think the government would not care if they are mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי מאיר discussion and returns to the wording of the משנה, starting a צריכא on its list of cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה needed to mention מדי and יון, since one might think kingdoms from the past do not bother the current government.

steps.title: Why the building of the בית המקדש must also be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only מדי and יון, one might say they are a problem because they were kingdoms. But dating by the building of the בית המקדש might seem harmless.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only the kingdom of מדי and the kingdom of יון, I would say that is a problem because they were kingdoms. But the building of the בית המקדש? What was, was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the צריכא. It explains why the case of dating by the building of the בית המקדש also had to be stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מדי and יון were real rival kingdoms, so the current government could resent seeing them named. The building of the בית המקדש is not a kingdom at all, so one might think the government would not mind. The משנה teaches that it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Kingdoms
The building of the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מַלְכוּת מָדַי וּמַלְכוּת יָוָן –
phrases.english: And if it had taught us the kingdom of Media and the kingdom of Greece –
that is because they were kingdoms;
but the building of the Temple –
what was, was;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מַלְכוּת מָדַי וּמַלְכוּת יָוָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second link in the צריכא chain, moving from past kingdoms to the building of the בית המקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה needed to mention the building of the בית המקדש, since one might think a non-kingdom event from the past would not bother the government.

steps.title: Why the destruction of the בית המקדש must also be mentioned
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the building of the בית המקדש, one might say the government objects because Jews are praising themselves. But the destruction is a sad event, so one might think it is allowed. That is why every case is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught us only the building of the בית המקדש, I would say that is a problem because the government will say: 'They are mentioning their own praise.' But the destruction of the בית המקדש, which is a sorrow, I would say no, it is not a problem. So each case is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last link in the chain, explaining why the destruction of the בית המקדש also had to be stated. Then it closes: every case is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dating by the building of the בית המקדש could look like Jews celebrating their own glory instead of honoring the ruling government. The destruction is a painful memory, not something to boast about, so one might think the government would not mind. The משנה forbids it anyway, which completes the proof that no case in the list is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: They are mentioning their own praise
The destruction of the בית המקדש
Sorrow, pain
I would say no; one might think it is not included

steps.whatToRemember: Each dating case in the משנה (an illegitimate kingdom, מדי and יון, the building of the בית המקדש, its destruction) teaches something new. Any of them could have seemed harmless to the government, but all of them invalidate the גט.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us the building of the Temple –
that is because they will say: 'They are mentioning their own praise';
phrases.notes: 'They will say' means the government officials, who would feel the Jews are honoring their own past instead of the ruling power.

phrases.english: but the destruction of the Temple, which is a sorrow –
I would say no;
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final link of the צריכא chain, closing with the declaration that all the cases are needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All four dating cases in the משנה are needed, because each one could have seemed acceptable to the government for its own reason.

steps.title: Who was in the east?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of "he was in the east and wrote in the west" and asks who "he" is. It rules out the husband, because that case already appears elsewhere in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: "He was in the east and wrote in the west." Who is this? If you say it is the husband, then this is the same as the other case in the משנה: "He changed his name or her name, the name of his city or the name of her city"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and asks who it is talking about. It shows that the line cannot mean the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "he" were the בעל, then writing the wrong place for him would just be writing the wrong name of his city. The משנה already lists that case separately. A משנה does not repeat itself, so this line must be about someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: East
West
If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
That is the same as (points out that a case is a repeat)

phrases.english: He was in the east and wrote "in the west":
Who? If you say the husband,
phrases.notes: The question is who was really in the east: the husband or the scribe?

phrases.english: this is the same as "he changed his name or her name,
the name of his city or the name of her city"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing why each dating case in the משנה is needed, the גמרא moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose location is the משנה talking about in "he was in the east and wrote in the west"?

steps.title: It means the scribe, as רב taught his scribes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה is talking about the סופר, who wrote a different place from where he was sitting. רב and רב הונא told their scribes to always write the place where they were actually sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about the scribe? This is like what רב told his scribes, and רב הונא also told his scribes: When you are sitting in שילי, write "in שילי," even if the matter was given over to you in היני. And when you are sitting in היני, write "in היני," even if the matter was given over to you in שילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means the scribe. Then it brings the instructions of רב and רב הונא to show this kind of rule really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The place written in the document has to be where the סופר actually wrote it. Writing the place where the deal was arranged is wrong, even though it might seem connected to the document. That is the mistake in the משנה, and it makes the גט not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Scribe, the person who writes the document
His scribes
שילי, the name of a place
היני, the name of a nearby place
The matters were given over (the deal or instructions took place)

steps.whatToRemember: A document must give the place where the סופר actually wrote it, not the place where the deal was arranged. Writing the wrong place makes a גט not valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is to write where the deal happened. רב says the opposite: write where you are sitting while you write.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a practical rule for writing a גט and other documents: the place listed must match where the document is actually written.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not the scribe?
As Rav said to his scribes,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא לְסָפְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and similarly Rav Huna said to his scribes:
When you are sitting in Shili, write "in Shili";

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִימַּסְרָן לְכוּ מִילֵּי בְּהִינֵי.
phrases.english: even though the matters were given over to you in Hini.
And when you are sitting in Hini, write "in Hini";

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמִימַּסְרָן לְכוּ מִילֵּי בְּשִׁילֵי.
phrases.english: even though the matters were given over to you in Shili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 by choosing the scribe instead of the husband.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה means the סופר, who wrote a place other than where he was sitting. רב and רב הונא's instructions to their scribes support this.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The instructions of רב and רב הונא to their scribes about שילי and היני.

steps.title: Opening a new statement of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new statement that רב יהודה says in the name of שמואל. The statement itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring a new teaching from שמואל, and the teaching itself comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only tells us who is speaking: רב יהודה, passing on what he heard from his teacher שמואל. The content of the statement is not here yet, so the learner should get ready for the next move.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the clause about east and west, the גמרא begins a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the speakers are given here. שמואל's ruling, passed on by רב יהודה, comes next.
